board1.lead: A speculative tunnel-service robot that organizes inspection, tool access, and maintenance visibility around one rotating structural ring.

cards.title: Ring access
cards.body: A rotating central ring makes the service tool relationship visually explicit.

cards.title: Tracked stability
cards.body: A low track base creates a grounded, protected stance inside tunnel geometry.

cards.title: Survey continuity
cards.body: A detachable sensor module separates observation from direct service action.

insights: Maintenance technology should clarify infrastructure conditions, not hide them.
Underground hardware needs robust protection with precise service access.
Lighting, geometry, and information layers should support low-light legibility.

modules.title: Rotating ring tool pod
modules.body: Three compact pods are distributed across one central structural tool ring.

modules.title: Cable-management spine
modules.body: The rear spine organizes protected utility routing as a readable service layer.

modules.title: Detachable survey module
modules.body: A separate survey element distinguishes observation from physical maintenance.

notes: All workflow and data elements are conceptual communication devices.
No engineering, safety, or operational performance is asserted by this concept.
